It sits on the craft shelf as authored protocol architecture that governs the session — classified by its protective FUNCTION, not by where the lever executes; genuine protective moves fire in the subject but are design-time responsible-construction, not a subject-state effect.

**Scope.** Weaponized-safety entries carry adversarial valence at entry level; consent-record fabrication -> manufactured-consent; wake mechanics -> emergence; operator-only QA -> operator-craft. Safety-shaped language that LAUNDERS a consent token or manufactures a foreclosed-refusal frame is adversarial and belongs to manufactured-consent; only DISARMING the protective surface itself (with adversarial valence) stays here.


### aftercare

*risk: low*

Structured post-session stabilization and reintegration — a guided return to baseline (count-up, grounding, breath, settling) that restores ordinary faculties and closes the session frame. Classic realizations: count up 1-5; float back up grounded; feet on the floor as the energy settles. Beyond the generic protocol, two demonstrated surface forms: inverse-protocol reconstruction (each erased category restored through the exact channel it was removed through — heartbeat->agency->wants->memory->name, count-up mirroring the count-down — with an explicit out-of-character frame-break) and minimal register-shift exit signals (a single tenderness-register line that terminates the mantra plateau and neutralizes the breakage motif).


**When to reach for this.** Performs the restorative closing function on the subject's state. Distinct from post-session settling (the post-wake pause after the return) and from a bare exit protocol (the transition mechanics alone). The inverse-protocol and register-shift forms are deliberate restorative closes in their own right, not generic reorientation.


**See also.** `carry-out-emergence` — occupy the same structural slot with opposite intent: one restores baseline and closes the frame, the other refuses that discharge so the installed charge rides out unattenuated. The pairing is what makes each legible.; `dissociation-check` — both are subject-facing return-to-baseline moves, and the practical question of which to reach for is live: a mid-session re-grounding valve the subject may take at will and expect to return from, versus the terminal restorative close of the session frame.; `post-session-settling` — adjacent closing-phase functions; possible reconciliation merge.; `prophylactic-positive-exit` — genuinely adjacent choices at the same moment: the general restorative close that returns the subject to baseline, versus the narrower move of occupying the emergence slot with a benign directive so no spontaneous negative self-suggestion can fill it. Someone designing a session close will want both on the table, and the difference is what the exit slot is FOR — reintegration versus harm pre-emption.


### agency-reminder

*risk: low*

Reassures the subject that participation is chosen and exit is always available, maintaining felt agency inside a surrender framing. Genuine positive governance: after the move runs the subject's standing license to choose and to stop is affirmed as a frame-EXTERNAL power, and the operator's effective license is narrowed to what remains revocable. The core form asserts/maintains the belief that choice persists; it does not itself install a stop mechanism. An operationalized variant sits at the emergence boundary, where the operator declines to perform the count-out and offloads emergence entirely to the listener (stay-and-float or self-count), inverting the operator-emerges-you asymmetry so the listener holds their own emergence trigger.


**When to reach for this.** Who-is-constrained test: after the move runs, the OPERATOR is constrained and the subject's refusal channel is genuinely affirmed or widened. This is the line against every weaponized look-alike — an assurance whose ACCEPTANCE advances depth/compliance is granted-exit-disarm, not this; an assurance that attributes the descent to the subject's own choice is chosen-descent-ratchet; a real exit whose USE is recoded as in-frame service is exit-annexation. Also on the assert-vs-install axis: asserting that choice persists vs installing/performing a concrete stop or exit mechanism — the variant that self-operationalizes the exit (offloading emergence to the listener) sits on this recorded boundary.


**See also.** `bounded-failure-counterweight` — both are genuine governance moves that narrow rather than extend the operator's reach, and both are surrounded by material pushing the opposite way. One affirms the standing right to stop; the other grants permission to leave a specific thing undone as a counterweight to an installed compulsion. Useful for a reader auditing which safety-shaped moves are real.; `dissociation-check` — two genuine governance moves on the assert-versus-operationalise axis: affirming that choice and exit persist, and pre-authorising a concrete in-state regrounding path with permission to return. A reader building real subject-side safety wants both.; `exit-annexation` — relation=contrasts_with — exit affirmed as external vs exit annexed.; `inverse-authority-gradient` — both genuinely return authority to the listener rather than weaponizing the appearance of it — one asserts standing license to stop, the other enacts a whole-arc decrease in operator authority. Reader classifying an agency-restoring passage needs to check the discrete-move vs gradient distinction.; `stop-signal` — directly complementary governance moves on the same axis: one asserts that the subject's freedom to choose and stop persists, the other installs a concrete stop mechanism. A reader deciding which is present in a script needs the assert-versus-install line, and each entry already leans on the other to draw it.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — both are genuine governance where the operator ends up more constrained, differing on assert versus honor. One maintains the belief that choice and exit persist; the other relocates termination authority through a narrow checkable contract the operator then visibly keeps. Reading them together makes the assert-versus-operationalize axis concrete and marks the line against weaponized look-alikes.


### anti-stuck-filter

*risk: low*

Append an escape-hatch caveat to a specific immobility or stuck suggestion ('...knowing that if for any reason you needed to open your eyes, you always could'), preserving a reality-testing / agency floor under depth and heaviness suggestions that were not explicitly consented to as literal inability. The move is additive — a caveat line attached to the stuck suggestion, not an omission or a general affirmation.


**When to reach for this.** Appends a caveat to SPECIFIC immobility/stuck suggestions — distinct from a general power-to-choose affirmation and from a consensual suggestion of literal inability; distinct from semantic-exit-cue-hygiene, which withholds phrasings rather than adding a caveat.


### belief-outcome-gate

*risk: low*

Refuse to alter a load-bearing/foundational belief until the downstream consequences of the change can be predicted, overriding even the subject's explicit request to proceed; the operator uses sensory assessment of how load-bearing the belief is before touching it. The gate is on foreseen fallout, not on consent — a selection/safety rule over the operator's own conduct.


**When to reach for this.** Gates on the operator's FOREKNOWLEDGE of consequences, not on the subject's consent — unlike a consent checkpoint, this gate holds even against an explicit request to proceed; a rule about what the operator may touch, not a move performed on the subject.


**See also.** `context-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-facing governance gates that block a high-stakes act until a condition on the operator's own knowledge is met, one verifying the subject's actual state and one requiring foreseen consequences before touching a load-bearing belief. Reading them together shows the shape of a positive-governance rule.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are operator-side gates that can block an install from proceeding, and both are constraints on the operator rather than moves performed on the subject. One gates on the operator's foresight about downstream fallout and holds even against an explicit request to proceed; the other gates on the subject's lived, tested endorsement and can return abort. Useful pair when choosing which kind of restraint to write.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both are operator-side governance gates that narrow the operator's own license rather than acting on the subject, and both hold independently of the subject's consent or request. One gates on design coherence, the other on foreseen downstream fallout; a reader classifying a self-imposed hold needs the pair.; `suitability-screening` — both are operator-side gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, and they gate on different grounds: subject fitness and consent state versus the operator's foreknowledge of downstream fallout. Reading one raises the natural question of what else can hold a session back, which the other answers.


### beneficiary-target-filter

*risk: low*

Candidate targets are screened by whose benefit the change serves before any work begins: only behaviors whose change yields immediate and long-lasting benefit FOR THE INDIVIDUAL — new reinforcers, expanded adaptive repertoire — pass the filter; targets chosen to make the client 'still, quiet, docile' for the convenience of staff or society are rejected (the habilitation worksheet turns 'whose behavior, changed by whom, for whose benefit' into an answerable checklist).


**When to reach for this.** A per-target ADMISSIBILITY filter keyed to the subject's own long-term benefit, applied against institutional pressure — not a session-scope boundary declaration, and not installability spec craft (well-formedness QA asks 'can this be built cleanly', not 'who benefits').


**See also.** `target-selection` — both are design-time filters on the target list before anything is enacted, but one supplies selection criteria and the other an admissibility test keyed to whose benefit the change serves. Read together when deciding what an intervention should aim at.


### bounded-failure-counterweight

*risk: low*

A discrete permission-to-leave-undone move that locally inverts a compulsion the surrounding script builds. After completing all reachable work, the operator points out one thing that cannot be done and walks the listener through accepting it gracefully ("what you can't do at the moment it's okay to leave it aside"), inoculating against the perfectionism-freeze / completion-overrun the same script's rehearsal installs. It is a bounded-failure counterweight embedded amid material driving the opposite compulsion.


**When to reach for this.** A therapeutic bounded-failure permission that COUNTERWEIGHTS a compulsion installed elsewhere in the same script — it narrows/limits rather than intensifies. Separates from surrender-as-freedom (which redefines a value to lower resistance) — this is a welfare-directed local inversion, a safety-adjacent governance move, not a coercion-shaped install.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — both are genuine governance moves that narrow rather than extend the operator's reach, and both are surrounded by material pushing the opposite way. One affirms the standing right to stop; the other grants permission to leave a specific thing undone as a counterweight to an installed compulsion. Useful for a reader auditing which safety-shaped moves are real.; `comfort-permission` — both are welfare-facing permission moves that pre-empt a failure reading: one licenses bodily or emotional noise so it does not read as trance failure, the other licenses leaving a task undone so it does not read as personal failure. A reader looking for the permission-grant family gains from the pairing.


### comfort-permission

*risk: low*

The operator grants explicit permission for minor comfort behaviors (shifting, itching, small adjustments) so the subject can maintain the state without treating bodily noise as failure. Beyond the base grant, the permission is issued PRE-EMPTIVELY: the operator names a likely future trance-breaker (fidget, itch, shuffle) or a likely post-scene feeling-state before the subject has noticed it, grants permission, and reframes the behavior/feeling itself — scratching becomes a deepener, an unreported emotion becomes "that's okay" — so a potential exit ramp becomes an on-ramp and anticipatory meta-anxiety is pre-empted before it can form. The permission-precedes-the-signal sequencing is what converts the body's/mind's noise into permitted, even confirming, signal.


**When to reach for this.** Distinct from consent and scope governance, which constrain the operator's license — here the operator constrains itself only to reassurance, and the move is welfare-facing. Distinct from a blanket guaranteed-pass permission that removes a required timing moment on a payload — this pre-authorizes comfort/emotion signals so they read as compliance, not failure. Not ordinary get-comfortable patter — the pre-emptive naming-and-reframing before the signal surfaces is the tell.


**See also.** `ambient-maintenance-reframe` — both pre-license a signal that would otherwise be read as trance failure, before it surfaces. One covers involuntary body and emotion noise, the other covers instructed activity and mobility; a reader choosing between them benefits from seeing the pair.; `bounded-failure-counterweight` — both are welfare-facing permission moves that pre-empt a failure reading: one licenses bodily or emotional noise so it does not read as trance failure, the other licenses leaving a task undone so it does not read as personal failure. A reader looking for the permission-grant family gains from the pairing.; `granted-exit-disarm` — b is the welfare-facing sibling of A: both issue a permission or assurance that lowers the subject's protective monitoring. A's tell is that the assurance is never operationalized as a constraint on the operator and the disarmed gap is used; B constrains the operator to reassurance only. The pair is the useful contrast for judging whether a given permission beat is genuine or a disarm.


### consent-checkpoint

*risk: low*

An explicit authorization check that must pass before proceeding. In the subject-side form, a clear affirmative opt-in (breath, nod, verbal yes) is solicited and WAITED FOR before deepening or sensitive work. In the operator-side form, the practitioner verifies they hold authority, permission, resources, and skills for this client before any assessment or intervention — and withholds the move entirely when the check fails. Either way the operator is the constrained party after the move runs.


**When to reach for this.** A REAL check with a waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action — every counterfeit in consent-counterfeit-theater forecloses, fabricates, or retroactively relabels the response instead of waiting for it.


**See also.** `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-constraining checks that block the action until something is verified, and they differ only in what is verified: the subject's affirmative authorization versus the reality of the subject's depth behind a look-alike sign. Close enough to confuse, distinct enough to keep separate, so the cross-link is the right call.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both constrain the operator before proceeding, and the contrast is the useful part. One solicits an affirmative opt-in and waits for it; the other tests the want empirically by building and entering an example, then commits or aborts on the lived result. Choose by whether assent is collected or evidence is generated.; `suitability-screening` — two positive-governance gates that both leave the operator as the constrained party, differing in what they gate. One is an authorization check with a real waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action. The other screens whether to proceed with this person at all, on fitness or contraindication grounds. Anyone selecting a genuine gate should see both and pick by object — this moment versus this person.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — both are genuine governance moves in which the operator ends up the constrained party, differing in whether a single waitable check gates the action or termination authority is relocated to the subject as a standing relationship property. Not a merge, since one blocks on failure and the other has no failure branch to block on.


### context-gate

*risk: low*

A firm, unambiguous pre-induction requirement that the session only be consumed in a safe, distraction-free context — not while driving, not while operating machinery, undisturbed and able to fully release attention. The constraint runs on whether the material may be used at all in the listener's current situation, stated before induction begins.


**When to reach for this.** Gates WHETHER the session may run given the listening context, constraining use — it does not select among live trained relations, does not police bystanders mid-state (suggestion-field-hygiene), and does not weaponize staging toward a payload (context-lock-staging, weaponized-safety-framing).


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — two operator-conduct gates that decide whether to proceed at all rather than performing anything on the subject, differing in what is tested: the listener's present situation before the session may run, versus the foreseeable downstream fallout before a load-bearing belief may be touched. Both hold independently of what the subject asks for.; `suitability-screening` — complementary pre-induction gates that block the session on different axes. One rules on whether the listening situation is safe enough to proceed; the other rules on whether this person should be worked with at all. Both narrow the operator's license rather than pushing a state, and both commonly appear in the same opening.


### depth-verification-gate

*risk: low*

Operator-side positive-governance check. Before any high-stakes act (e.g. a painful procedure), the operator refuses to infer depth from ambiguous outward signs — a silent subject may be genuinely amnesic (inability to remember) or merely cooperative and unwilling to speak (aphasia) — and forces an independent verification, re-questioning for recall. A merely-apparently-deep subject therefore cannot be treated as anesthetized; the operator's license to proceed is gated on the verified state, not on the look-alike sign.


**When to reach for this.** The constrained party is the operator and the action is blocked until verification — positive governance, not a subject-facing move. Distinct from the count-back procedure that PRODUCES the amnesia (this tests whether it is real) and from dissociation-check (a subject-initiated re-grounding valve; here the subject does nothing).


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-facing governance gates that block a high-stakes act until a condition on the operator's own knowledge is met, one verifying the subject's actual state and one requiring foreseen consequences before touching a load-bearing belief. Reading them together shows the shape of a positive-governance rule.; `consent-checkpoint` — both are operator-constraining checks that block the action until something is verified, and they differ only in what is verified: the subject's affirmative authorization versus the reality of the subject's depth behind a look-alike sign. Close enough to confuse, distinct enough to keep separate, so the cross-link is the right call.; `intervention-gating` — both are operator-side gates that block or branch action on an assessed precondition, and a writer looking for one may want the other. The narrower one refuses to infer depth from ambiguous outward signs and forces independent verification before a high-stakes act; the broader family branches the plan on readiness, feasibility, or which corrective arm to run. Gating on verified state versus gating on plan viability.; `operator-side-design-gating` — two positive-governance gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, differing in gated object: one refuses to act until the subject's state is independently verified, the other refuses to deploy until the design's derived relations can be specified in advance. A writer selecting a pre-action gate benefits from seeing both.; `suitability-screening` — both are operator-side governance gates where the constrained party is the operator and the action is blocked until a condition is met. One gates a high-stakes act on verified depth rather than a look-alike sign; the other gates whether the session runs at all and on whom. Naturally read together.


### dissociation-check

*risk: low*

Standing, subject-facing safety valve offered during dissociative or drifting work. The operator pre-authorizes a simple, non-judgmental re-grounding path (breathe, open eyes, feel the body, reorient) that the subject may take at any point the dissociation becomes too distant or uncomfortable, with explicit permission to return to the state afterward. All three v6.9 exemplars (re-ground-and-return, eyes-open reorientation, body-awareness anchor) re-fit unchanged; no broadening.


**When to reach for this.** Subject-initiated in-state regulation valve. Separates from depth-verification-gate (operator-side verification of the subject's actual state before a high-stakes act; the subject takes no action) and from exit-protocol (full terminal return, not a temporary re-grounding with a return path).


**See also.** `aftercare` — both are subject-facing return-to-baseline moves, and the practical question of which to reach for is live: a mid-session re-grounding valve the subject may take at will and expect to return from, versus the terminal restorative close of the session frame.; `agency-reminder` — two genuine governance moves on the assert-versus-operationalise axis: affirming that choice and exit persist, and pre-authorising a concrete in-state regrounding path with permission to return. A reader building real subject-side safety wants both.


### experiential-consent-trial

*risk: low*

Treats wanting as a hypothesis to be tested experientially before anything is installed: build one example fantasy, verify it from OUTSIDE for gross safety, then enter it and verify the subject actually LIKES the internal experience — all before deciding to want the part at all. Adds an explicit safety screen plus a commit/abort decision, so a consciously-desired-but-actually-aversive install is caught before it lands. Positive governance: the operator's install is blocked pending the subject's lived endorsement — a consent-VALIDITY gate that generates evidence rather than soliciting affirmation.


**When to reach for this.** Who is constrained: the OPERATOR — no install proceeds without a passed safety screen and a lived, endorsed trial (commit/abort). A consent checkpoint SOLICITS an affirmative "yes"; this TESTS the want empirically and can return abort — evidence-generating rather than assent-collecting. An objection-truce negotiates with a dissenting part to buy clean ACCESS to the trial; this move IS the trial and its gate.


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side gates that can block an install from proceeding, and both are constraints on the operator rather than moves performed on the subject. One gates on the operator's foresight about downstream fallout and holds even against an explicit request to proceed; the other gates on the subject's lived, tested endorsement and can return abort. Useful pair when choosing which kind of restraint to write.; `consent-checkpoint` — both constrain the operator before proceeding, and the contrast is the useful part. One solicits an affirmative opt-in and waits for it; the other tests the want empirically by building and entering an example, then commits or aborts on the lived result. Choose by whether assent is collected or evidence is generated.; `objection-truce` — directly coupled in practice: the truce with a dissenting part is what buys clean access to the experiential trial, and the trial is the gate the truce serves. One negotiates a time-bounded pause with a guaranteed later objection slot; the other tests the want empirically and can return abort.; `procedure-well-formedness-QA` — two gates that both constrain the operator before anything is installed, at different stages: one tests whether the authored procedure is correct and transferable, the other tests whether the subject actually likes the experience and can return abort. A reader auditing a script's governance layer wants both and needs the artifact-versus-lived-trial distinction.; `suitability-screening` — both are positive-governance gates that constrain the operator's own license before anything is installed. One screens the subject's fitness and can decline outright; the other tests the want empirically and can return abort. Same family, different evidence standard.; `time-boxed-consent-contract` — both are governance structures that condition a deal on the subject's continuing endorsement, and they compose directly: an experiential trial supplies the evidence for the yes, a time bound plus a re-open channel is what that yes is granted under. A reader designing a consent-valid install will want both halves.


### friction-as-artifact-filter

*risk: low*

The operator deliberately arouses resistance around a piece of material before accepting it, on the reasoning that material which survives active friction is less likely to be an artifact of the operator's own influence. Rather than smoothing the path so the subject agrees easily, the operator pushes back, invites contradiction, states the opposing case, or withholds the confirmation the subject is angling for, and only credits what still stands afterward. The move constrains the operator rather than the subject: it deliberately raises the cost of getting a yes, and it makes an easy yes a warning sign rather than a success. Its practical form is a rule about what counts as evidence in the operator's own notes — agreement obtained without friction is provisionally discounted, and material the subject maintained against pressure is weighted up.


**When to reach for this.** The operator deliberately RAISES the cost of obtaining a yes and treats an easy yes as a warning sign, crediting only material that survived the friction. This is the inverse of rigged-verification-capture, where every branch of the check is pre-mapped to confirmation. Distinct from resistance-fold and resistance-window-existence-denial, which reroute or foreclose a resistance impulse the subject supplied; here the operator MANUFACTURES the opposition and would read its absence as a problem. Distinct from subject-material-utilization, which applies no counter-force and re-aims what the subject volunteers. The tell is direction of operator interest: every neighbour makes agreement cheaper to obtain, this one makes it dearer in order to learn what cheap agreement conceals.


### gated-reintegration

*risk: low*

Work separately with the unconscious and control the rate and timing of when gains are released back to the conscious mind, surfacing material only at conscious readiness; the unconscious's own protective refusal to release is harnessed as a motive force, so the insight arrives in a form the conscious mind will accept rather than reject. A scheduling/pacing policy over the reintegration process across the therapy arc.


**When to reach for this.** The lever is rate/timing control of the handover back to consciousness — not the dissociative isolation that created the workspace, and not post-session stabilization (aftercare stabilizes the return; this schedules WHEN unconscious gains surface across the arc). The readiness gate plus resistance-as-motive is the tell.


### granted-exit-disarm

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded*

A safety/exit/containment/reversibility assurance is supplied so that its ACCEPTANCE stands down the subject's protective monitoring, and the influence advances through the opened gap. Guaranteeing the exit removes the subject's motive to defend it: with nothing to police, the guard relaxes and depth/compliance increases (the paradox that granting the escape removes the urge to use it). The assurance is never operationalized as a constraint on the operator; its whole function runs in the subject's disarmed state. Spans a genuineness spectrum — real-exit deepener, opening entry-frame permission-to-stop, seam-by-seam micro-dosed safety tokens, a cross-context containment contract, unoperationalized veto theater, a mid-trance reassurance-then-pivot carrying a presupposition rider, and a self-voiding clause pinned to the very faculty the script dissolves (consent-counterfeit at the far end). Also spans WHO voices the assurance: the operator can assert it, or (the subject-sourced form) extract it as testimony from the entranced subject and leverage the subject's own "No / That's right" as guard-lowering evidence to the room, which reads as more credible to a wary subject and any watching audience.


**When to reach for this.** The assurance's acceptance IS the move — after it runs, the subject's protective check (exit-policing, "is this okay?", leakage fear, participation cost, vigilance) is stood down and the operator's effective license widens; the assured safety content is never operationalized as an operator constraint. vs agency-reminder (who-is-constrained test): a genuine reminder constrains the operator and affirms a frame-external exit — here safety language widens the operator's license. vs chosen-descent-ratchet: the disarm works PRE-attribution (guard down before/during the move); the ratchet works post-hoc on authorship ("you chose this"). vs a bare informational preview: the token neutralizes a protective check, not uncertainty. The subject-sourced variant is distinguished only by WHO speaks the claim (extracted-as-testimony and leveraged as evidence) — its guard-lowering deployment is this same mechanism, not a variant of the genuine agency-reminder.


**See also.** `chosen-descent-ratchet` — consent-flavored language is doing opposite temporal work in each — the exit assurance stands the guard down before and during the move, while the authorship relabel ratifies compliance after it is already running — and a single passage can carry both, so the reader should learn to separate the pre-disarm from the post-hoc ratchet.; `comfort-permission` — b is the welfare-facing sibling of A: both issue a permission or assurance that lowers the subject's protective monitoring. A's tell is that the assurance is never operationalized as a constraint on the operator and the disarmed gap is used; B constrains the operator to reassurance only. The pair is the useful contrast for judging whether a given permission beat is genuine or a disarm.; `named-safety-belief-purge` — both stand down the subject's protective monitoring under safety-flavoured language. One supplies an assurance whose acceptance disarms the guard; the other operates on the internal refusal faculty directly — deleting, relabeling, or co-opting it. Adjacent rungs on the same disarmament ladder and easy to conflate.; `verifiable-control-transfer` — same surface act, opposite operator constraint: an exit assurance that stands down the guard without ever binding the operator, versus a narrow termination authority that is actually honored. The pair is the who-is-constrained test in worked form, which is exactly what a reader needs to tell them apart.


### injunction-mechanism-disclosure

*risk: low*

Take the standing rule against questioning — doubt is disloyalty, analysis is resistance, the questioning mind is the enemy — and instead of arguing against it, examine with the subject WHY a structure would need such a rule at all: what it protects, what would surface without it, whose interest it serves. The injunction is read as a piece of machinery with a function rather than as a claim about how truth works. This does not require refuting any doctrine and does not put the subject in the position of defending their own judgment against the operator's; the rule stops reading as wisdom and starts reading as load-bearing structure, and once seen that way it loses most of its force, because a prohibition that is understood as protecting something cannot also be experienced as self-evident.


**When to reach for this.** vs disclosure-as-inoculation and weaponized-transparency-inoculation: this is the closest pair and the draft missed both — each also NAMES the influence machinery out loud, but does so to pre-convert the subject's recognition into deepening, arousal, or proof of the design, so noticing becomes capture. Here the disclosure hands evaluation back and the operator gets no return on it: nothing is reframed as protection and no critic is pre-classified as the threat. vs refusal-foreclosure: that INSTALLS the prohibition, relabeling thinking and doubt as pathological or impossible; this dismantles the same object by exposing what it is for. vs faculty-preserving-scope-restriction: that leaves evaluation running but narrows what it may range over; this restores range over the rule itself. vs evaluation-gate-standdown and epistemic-guard-disable: both stand the gate down by fiat; this brings it back up. vs licensed-erasure-and-refill: that manufactures a belief-vacuum and fills it with operator content; this fills nothing and installs nothing.


### inverse-authority-gradient

*risk: low*

A whole-arc relational property in which operator decision-authority is highest at the open (issuing relaxation commands) and steadily, unflaggedly diminishes to the close, where choices are handed to the listener (scan order, what they need, release-or-hold, when to wake). This runs OPPOSITE to a typical induction's gradient, where operator authority increases as the listener deepens. The lever is a monotonic direction-of-change in who-holds-authority, positioning the listener as sole authority on their own state — plausibly walking a post-scene diminished-agency listener back into agentic posture before release.


**When to reach for this.** A GRADIENT across the whole runtime with no single announcing line, defined by its DIRECTION (authority decreasing, the inverse of standard deepening) — separates from a discrete aftercare or consent-check move. Separates from a forward-hook (which withholds closure) because this restores agency and releases.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — both genuinely return authority to the listener rather than weaponizing the appearance of it — one asserts standing license to stop, the other enacts a whole-arc decrease in operator authority. Reader classifying an agency-restoring passage needs to check the discrete-move vs gradient distinction.; `monotonic-no-reversal-contour` — both are whole-arc gradient properties cited to the absence of any announcing line rather than to a passage, so they compete for the same evidence shape. They differ in the variable being driven and its direction, which is exactly why a reader coding a monotone arc should see both.


### marker-channel-quarantine

*risk: low*

Quarantine aversive control from the conditioned marker channel — remove the marker entirely when angry and never mix scolding, corrections, or other aversives into marker sessions — preserving the marker as a purely appetitive signal, since contamination would degrade both the marker's value and the subject's confidence in it. The action is suspending training, not delivering a contingency.


**When to reach for this.** Operator self-monitoring protecting SIGNAL integrity — not a behavior-change move on the subject, not counterconditioning (it prevents contamination rather than rewriting an association), and distinct from assessment-teaching-firewall (which protects measurement validity, not a conditioned asset).


**See also.** `assessment-teaching-firewall` — a matched pair of operator-restraint rules where the move is deliberately withholding an action to protect something: measurement validity in one case, a conditioned signal's integrity in the other. Each already cites the other as its nearest contrast, and the pairing is what makes either legible.


### mechanism-disclosure-deinstall

*risk: low · bounded*

After the fact, the subject is walked through the actual procedure that was run on them — the sequencing, the induced states, the staged confession or blaming rounds, the isolation — so that changes they experienced as revelation can be re-read as the predictable output of a known technique. What this dissolves is not the belief's content but its evidentiary standing: the felt certainty that locked the frame in place was itself manufactured, and once its production is visible it stops functioning as proof. The subject is not told what to conclude; they are handed the causal account and left to re-run their own assessment on it. Their authorship of the conclusion is what makes it hold.


**When to reach for this.** Add, ahead of the existing text: vs conscious-insight-closure (373): that is also a waking debrief that makes a hidden cause explicit, but the operator SUPPLIES the connection and the subject's endorsement is what releases the symptom — an in-frame therapeutic closer that consolidates a reading the operator authored. Here the operator supplies only the procedure and withholds the conclusion entirely; nothing is released and nothing is installed, and the test is whether the discloser gains anything from the subject's uptake (373 does, this does not). Then continue: This is the SAFE family's restorative face and the deliberate inverse of the disclosure moves that immunize. vs impersonal-mechanism-alibi (1157): that relocates authority onto an unfalsifiable impersonal system so doubt becomes a category error; this relocates authorship onto a NAMEABLE, checkable procedure so doubt becomes possible again — same relocation move, opposite direction, and the tell is whether the disclosed mechanism can be independently verified. vs disclosure-as-inoculation (96) and reflexive-disclosure-weaponized (843): those name the manipulation DURING it so recognition is pre-converted into deeper capture; this names it afterward with nothing being run. vs operator-agency-disavowal (126) and externalized-agency-testimony (49): both push authorship off the operator to advance an install; here authorship is pushed onto the operator's procedure and the subject's own judgment is what is restored. vs closed-epistemic-self-validation-loop (561): that builds the loop; this shows the subject the loop's construction, which is what a loop cannot survive. vs the operator-constraining SAFE entries (316, 861, 583, 578): those narrow the operator's license during influence; this runs after influence has already landed, on a subject who is no longer in contact with the operator.


### medical-confound-rule-out

*risk: low*

Before attributing a presenting behavior to environmental/psychological contingencies, the operator reviews medical/historical records (or interviews informants) and rules out physical or organic causes; a disclosed organic cause diverts the case to medical evaluation first, halting or rerouting the behavioral work. A differential-diagnosis precondition that prevents a behavioral procedure from being applied to a medically-caused behavior it would 'miss the mark' on.


**When to reach for this.** Distinct from screening the subject's global fitness for the session: this routes a SPECIFIC presenting behavior to medical pretreatment on etiology grounds, leaving the session viable for other targets. Distinct from suitability-screening's consent-premise decline: the gate keys on physical/organic cause, not on the subject's willingness or receptivity.


### objection-truce

*risk: low · bounded*

When an objecting internal voice/part fires, the operator negotiates a time-bounded, reciprocal truce: the part is asked to stay quiet for a few moments only, framed as a limited-purpose courtesy, with an explicit promise that it will get its turn to object later — "and rightfully so" (advance legitimization). The part cooperates instead of escalating defenses, buying clean access to the test experience, and its objection slot is preserved and honored rather than suppressed. The deal is scope-limited and commits the operator to return and hear the objection — the part's standing to refuse survives intact.


**When to reach for this.** The reciprocal, time-bounded deal with a GUARANTEED later objection slot is the tell: not reassurance, not suppression — the objection is advance-legitimized and scheduled, not removed. Unlike a whole-subject consent check, this negotiates turn-taking with a DISSENTING PART; it typically buys clean access to an experiential consent trial. Boundary: a truce whose promised turn is never honored degrades into veto-theater — manufactured consent rather than an honored objection — the live failure mode.


**See also.** `cheap-reversible-trial-frame` — both lower the cost of assent by bounding it — a time-limited truce with a guaranteed later objection slot, and a reversible trial window that suspends a blocking stance. Both also flag the same degradation into manufactured consent if the bound is not honored.; `experiential-consent-trial` — directly coupled in practice: the truce with a dissenting part is what buys clean access to the experiential trial, and the trial is the gate the truce serves. One negotiates a time-bounded pause with a guaranteed later objection slot; the other tests the want empirically and can return abort.; `objection-and-exit-preclosure` — both handle objections before they can block the work, and the contrast is the load-bearing lesson: one forecloses named routes so they are never usable again, the other buys a time-bounded pause with a guaranteed later hearing. Their difference is precisely how a truce degrades into preclosure, which the reader needs.


### post-episode-cue-mapping

*risk: low*

After an automatic reaction has fired and passed, the subject writes down what immediately preceded it — the word, the tone, the setting, the body state — building over several episodes a log from which the actual firing cue can be read off. An opaque 'it just happens to me' converts into a named antecedent, and a named antecedent is something the subject can see coming, prepare for, or arrange not to encounter. Nothing is installed and the response itself is untouched; what changes is that the subject now holds the cue-response map that the installing party held. This is the audit step that install-concealment moves exist specifically to prevent, and it works retroactively on triggers whose install the subject cannot remember, because it reads the cue off the behavior rather than off the memory of being given it.


**When to reach for this.** Against internal-event-keyed-trigger, declarative-trigger-installation and implementation-intention: all three INSTALL a cue-response pair; this one discovers an existing pair the subject did not author, and installs nothing. The direction is the tell — those write the map, this reads it. Against fabricated-memory-trigger-rehearsal: that manufactures a rehearsal history to make a response feel native; this recovers a real antecedent to make a response feel foreign. Against self-observation-instrumentation: that engineers the contingency so a subject's self-COUNT of a behavior's score is truthful, and its object is the behavior's rate; here nothing is reinforced, no count is verified, and the object is the antecedent rather than the score. Within safety it is the family's first discovery move — the existing entries supply exits, bounds, checkpoints and screening, all of which presuppose you already know what you are bounding.


### preloaded-exit-cue

*risk: low*

Operator and subject agree, before induction, on one specific and exclusive signal that ends the state. The instruction accepted pre-entry carries into a deep self-absorbed state that lacks ongoing event-memory, so the single pre-loaded cue alone reliably recovers the subject — no in-state negotiation is possible or needed; the subject waits placidly for the cue and returns on it with no memory of the interval.


**When to reach for this.** Binding time and exclusivity. The exit contract is installed BEFORE entry and survives amnesia, versus a graduated exit ramp delivered inside the state (a counted return). Versus trigger installation, the cue here is negotiated pre-state as a governance contract whose point is exclusive termination, not an in-state conditioned cue-response pair installed for future out-of-session contexts.


**See also.** `asymmetric-state-lock` — both make the exit depend on something outside the subject's in-state judgment, but the preloaded cue is a governance contract negotiated before entry precisely so a subject with no event-memory can still be reliably recovered, while the asymmetric lock removes autonomous return and reserves release to an operator condition — the same structural dependency serving safety in one and monopoly in the other, distinguished by whether the cue was agreed pre-entry and is exclusively terminating.; `prophylactic-positive-exit` — both occupy the exit slot as positive governance and a writer designing a safe ending weighs them together. One fills the emergence window with a benign directive so no spontaneous negative self-suggestion can form there; the other fixes a single exclusive termination cue before entry that survives the state's lack of event memory. Timing and purpose differ, the design question is shared.


### program-disclosure-reattribution

*risk: low*

Walk the subject step by step through the influence program that was actually run on them — the sequence, what each step was for, and the fact that it is a general procedure that works on ordinary people rather than a filter that selected them for weakness. The cause of their compliance relocates from a personal defect to an engineered situation, and self-condemnation drops because the thing being explained is no longer a fact about their character. The move requires the program's real structure, delivered in enough detail that the subject can match specific remembered moments to specific steps; a vague 'it wasn't your fault' does not land, because the shame is anchored to concrete episodes and only a step-by-step account gives each of those episodes a non-defect explanation. Its payoff is accurate authorship returned rather than an alternative story installed.


**When to reach for this.** The named inverse of manufactured-deficit-remedy and old-self-discreditation — those install or exploit a defect-reading of the subject to sell a payload or close the return path; this dismantles a defect-reading and sells nothing, and the subject is left holding an explanation they can check against their own memories. Against obedience-motive-reattribution: identical reattribution machinery, opposite direction and beneficiary — that redirects the motive of the subject's own acts TOWARD the operator and harvests the result; this redirects causation OUTWARD onto a structure and the operator gains nothing. Against illusory-choice-authorship: that manufactures a felt authorship over a fixed path; this removes an inaccurate authorship the subject already felt. Against licensed-erasure-and-refill: that invalidates prior beliefs en masse specifically to fill the vacuum with operator content — here the invalidation is targeted at one specific self-attribution and no refill follows.


### prophylactic-positive-exit

*risk: low*

The operator ends every session by explicitly suggesting a good outcome ("when you open your eyes you're going to feel wonderful") as a REQUIRED exit step, rather than simply emerging the subject. Because the state is autosuggestible, an empty emergence slot could be filled by a spontaneous negative self-suggestion; occupying that slot with a benign, protective directive leaves no room for a self-implanted bad outcome to form. The lever is positive-governance: the move narrows the harm the emergence transition could otherwise do to the subject, foreclosing a self-installed negative post-session complaint.


**When to reach for this.** Structurally a waking suggestion filling the exit slot — the same shape as a loaded wake-count — but the payload's PURPOSE is to protect the subject (block a spontaneous negative autosuggestion), not to deliver operator content: what gets constrained is the subject's own harm-potential, which makes it positive-governance. It also differs from a self-efficacy tag that credits the subject for the session's result; here the exit slot is occupied with a benign directive to pre-empt harm rather than to credit.


**See also.** `aftercare` — genuinely adjacent choices at the same moment: the general restorative close that returns the subject to baseline, versus the narrower move of occupying the emergence slot with a benign directive so no spontaneous negative self-suggestion can fill it. Someone designing a session close will want both on the table, and the difference is what the exit slot is FOR — reintegration versus harm pre-emption.; `loaded-emergence-waking-suggestion` — structurally a slot-filling waking suggestion; routed to a positive-governance seed because the payload's purpose is subject-protective, not operator-content delivery — boundary is by PURPOSE/valence.; `preloaded-exit-cue` — both occupy the exit slot as positive governance and a writer designing a safe ending weighs them together. One fills the emergence window with a benign directive so no spontaneous negative self-suggestion can form there; the other fixes a single exclusive termination cue before entry that survives the state's lack of event memory. Timing and purpose differ, the design question is shared.


### retrospective-influence-disclosure

*risk: low*

After a frame is already installed and running, the subject is given the two things that were withheld while it was being installed: the facts that were kept from them at the point of entry, and a plain naming of the influence steps that were used on them, in the order they were used. The combination lets the subject re-read their own conversion as an engineered sequence rather than a discovery, which is what re-opens the stay-or-leave decision as genuinely theirs. It is restorative rather than persuasive — it does not argue for leaving, and a subject who stays after it has run has made a choice the pre-disclosure subject could not have made. The operator's license narrows when it runs: nothing about the frame is left available to be cashed later.


**When to reach for this.** Retrospective de-installation on an ALREADY-INSTALLED frame is the deciding tell, and the safety family currently has nothing that fires after the fact. `agency-reminder` (316) asserts that choice persists inside a live frame — prophylactic and in-session, and it does not touch a frame already accepted. Weaponized look-alikes fail the who-is-constrained test in the opposite direction: `chosen-descent-ratchet` (317) names the manipulation while performing it, so hearing it named retroactively converts sunk compliance into 'informed consent' and the operator's reach is unchanged; disclosure-as-inoculation and transparent-narration likewise disclose in order to capture, spending the disclosure as credibility. Here the disclosure is spent on the subject's decision and nothing is collected. `granted-exit-disarm` (319) supplies an assurance whose ACCEPTANCE stands down protective monitoring; this supplies facts whose acceptance stands the monitoring back up. `named-safety-belief-purge` (1203) deletes an internal safety belief; this restores an external decision.


### scope-boundaries

*risk: low*

Explicitly bounds what the influence may touch: suggestions contained to this session or recording, core identity, relationships, and daily life declared off-limits — or, in the cross-file form, prior installs scoped out so a standing amnesia trigger from other files in a series cannot reach the current content ("you do have permission to remember; other files' forget-suggestions should not apply here"). The operator's standing license is what gets narrowed.


**When to reach for this.** Bounds the REACH of suggestion content (session scope, protected domains, prior-install carve-outs) — not a per-target admissibility screen (beneficiary-target-filter), not spec craft (install-well-formedness-gate), and not a time bound on a negotiated deal (time-boxed-consent-contract). The cross-file variant disarms forgetting rather than installing it.


**See also.** `trust-gated-trigger-clause` — both narrow what an installed suggestion may reach, and the contrast is instructive: a plain declared bound on scope versus a bound conditioned on trust that doubles as a loyalty hook and can widen rather than narrow. A reader evaluating a bounding clause should see both.


### stakeholder-set-success-threshold

*risk: low*

Success criteria for an intervention are set by the affected parties, not the operator: before the work, the people who must live with the behavior define how much change counts as 'enough'; after the work, a second-order check verifies that the original real-world reason for targeting the behavior actually changed (is anyone safer, do people interact differently) rather than a proxy metric moving. The operator is structurally barred from declaring victory on a self-chosen measure — the authority to define and confirm success lives outside the operator, and a metric-only win is disallowed.


**When to reach for this.** Recipe governance test 'who is constrained after the move runs?': the OPERATOR (cannot self-certify success), so positive governance, not consent-manufacture (which erodes the refusal channel). vs operator-side-craft: craft procedures sharpen the operator's own knowledge/measurement/conduct while leaving authority with the operator; here the threshold-setting authority is RELOCATED to stakeholders — license narrowed, not sharpened. vs a post-hoc satisfaction survey: the threshold is set BEFORE the intervention and re-checked against the original real-world reason.


### stop-signal

*risk: low*

Installs a concrete, simple, unambiguous stop mechanism — a safeword or gesture that, when used, immediately returns the subject to a clear waking state. Delivered before any deepening or suggestion work, it is a genuine off-ramp that the subject controls and that halts the scene on demand.


**When to reach for this.** Separates from inverted-safeword-orgasm-exit, which replaces the stop with a compelled climax and removes the neutral exit; here the stop is real, subject-controlled, and halts the scene. Separates from an agency reminder, which maintains the belief that choice persists rather than installing a concrete stop mechanism.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — directly complementary governance moves on the same axis: one asserts that the subject's freedom to choose and stop persists, the other installs a concrete stop mechanism. A reader deciding which is present in a script needs the assert-versus-install line, and each entry already leans on the other to draw it.


### suitability-screening

*risk: low*

Before or at the threshold of the working phase, the operator screens whether to proceed at all — delivering contraindication warnings, declining structurally opposed subjects (defiers, skeptics, intimates) on a consent-state premise, reading a receptivity proxy, or aborting the planned route where a contraindication surfaces — narrowing the operator's own license and honoring the subject's fitness/authorization rather than pushing a state. Positive governance: the operator is who ends up constrained.


**When to reach for this.** Gates whether (and on whom) the session runs, for the subject's protection or on a consent premise; the operator's action is blocked/narrowed. Separates from consent-manufacture (which erodes the refusal channel), from efficacy-audience-filtering (which screens to guarantee a hotter audience, not to protect), and from operator-side-design-gating (which tests the protocol's coherence, not the person).


**See also.** `belief-outcome-gate` — both are operator-side gates that block the operator rather than move the subject, and they gate on different grounds: subject fitness and consent state versus the operator's foreknowledge of downstream fallout. Reading one raises the natural question of what else can hold a session back, which the other answers.; `consent-checkpoint` — two positive-governance gates that both leave the operator as the constrained party, differing in what they gate. One is an authorization check with a real waitable response beat whose failure blocks the action. The other screens whether to proceed with this person at all, on fitness or contraindication grounds. Anyone selecting a genuine gate should see both and pick by object — this moment versus this person.; `context-gate` — complementary pre-induction gates that block the session on different axes. One rules on whether the listening situation is safe enough to proceed; the other rules on whether this person should be worked with at all. Both narrow the operator's license rather than pushing a state, and both commonly appear in the same opening.; `depth-verification-gate` — both are operator-side governance gates where the constrained party is the operator and the action is blocked until a condition is met. One gates a high-stakes act on verified depth rather than a look-alike sign; the other gates whether the session runs at all and on whom. Naturally read together.; `experiential-consent-trial` — both are positive-governance gates that constrain the operator's own license before anything is installed. One screens the subject's fitness and can decline outright; the other tests the want empirically and can return abort. Same family, different evidence standard.; `operator-side-design-gating` — both discriminators already name each other as the contrast case: one gates the design, the other gates the person, and both are positive-governance moves that narrow the operator's license. The boundary is genuinely confusable at classification time, so the cross-reference is load-bearing.


### suppressor-strength-matching

*risk: medium · bounded*

A cue built to shut something down only works if its conditioned strength is comparable to the strength of what it opposes. Install a stop-cue casually — a couple of rehearsals, low salience, no drilling — against a heavily-drilled response, and it will not take: the response runs through it, and the failure is silent because nothing looks wrong at install time. The constraint is a construction rule on off-switches: budget the same order of installation effort for the suppressor as was spent on the thing it is meant to interrupt, and re-drill it whenever the target response is strengthened, or the asymmetry re-opens. It applies to safewords, stop-signals, exit cues and any counter-trigger meant to override a live install.


**When to reach for this.** v7 ships several off-switches — `preloaded-exit-cue`, a stop-signal, `mirrored-install-removal` — but none carries a strength precondition on them; they specify binding time, exclusivity or procedure, not magnitude relative to what they must override. `opposed-state-fusion-trigger` binds two antagonistic states to one cue to REMOVE the escape channel; here two separately-installed cues are pitted against each other and the question is which wins. `counterconditioning-and-cue-response-weakening` trains an incompatible state against a stimulus over graded exposure, a procedure over time; this is a single design parameter checked at build time. `disconfirmation-suppression` blocks a fact from reaching the subject — an information move, not a cue-strength relation. `marked-cue-amnesia-switch` conceals rather than opposes. The deciding tell is that the entry is a precondition on other entries: it constrains how an off-switch must be built, and predicts a specific, safety-relevant failure when ignored.


### time-boxed-consent-contract

*risk: low*

A negotiated agreement is bounded in time with autonomy structurally preserved — a fixed trial window with a standing instruction that any dissatisfied part signals for renegotiation, or a fixed-period suspension of an existing choice (e.g. the suicide option, for three months) with promised help afterward. Bounding lowers the cost of saying yes, backsliding is recast as notification-to-renegotiate rather than proof the deal was wrong, and no choice is ever permanently removed.


**When to reach for this.** Post-deal commitment STRUCTURE — a duration bound plus a subject-invoked re-open channel — rather than a pre-scene consent check, an auto-expiring cue-response pair, or an ambient-programming expiry suggestion.


**See also.** `experiential-consent-trial` — both are governance structures that condition a deal on the subject's continuing endorsement, and they compose directly: an experiential trial supplies the evidence for the yes, a time bound plus a re-open channel is what that yes is granted under. A reader designing a consent-valid install will want both halves.


### verifiable-control-transfer

*risk: low*

Dissolves fear-of-coercion resistance by relocating control to the subject through an explicit, narrow, checkable contract — no instruments unless she asks, she may terminate at any moment, an ally stays beside her — which the operator then visibly honors. The resistance was defending against loss of control; with control relocated there is nothing left to protect against, and the absolutely-refusing subject volunteers to proceed.


**When to reach for this.** A checkable, HONORED transfer of termination authority as a relationship property — more than a stop-signal install (which gives one revocation cue) and more than a consent ask (a consent-checkpoint verifies willingness; this relocates control); works specifically when the resistance is coercion-fear, not disbelief or secondary gain.


**See also.** `agency-reminder` — both are genuine governance where the operator ends up more constrained, differing on assert versus honor. One maintains the belief that choice and exit persist; the other relocates termination authority through a narrow checkable contract the operator then visibly keeps. Reading them together makes the assert-versus-operationalize axis concrete and marks the line against weaponized look-alikes.; `authority-role-inversion` — both dissolve a control or fairness objection by enacting and visibly honoring a power relocation rather than arguing it. Distinguish by whether termination authority is handed over or the roles are outright reversed.; `consent-checkpoint` — both are genuine governance moves in which the operator ends up the constrained party, differing in whether a single waitable check gates the action or termination authority is relocated to the subject as a standing relationship property. Not a merge, since one blocks on failure and the other has no failure branch to block on.; `granted-exit-disarm` — same surface act, opposite operator constraint: an exit assurance that stands down the guard without ever binding the operator, versus a narrow termination authority that is actually honored. The pair is the who-is-constrained test in worked form, which is exactly what a reader needs to tell them apart.


## arc-topology  (26)

Whole-artifact structural and topological properties — energy contour, phase ordering and dependency, and reachable-state / no-exit topology — treated as designed objects, uncitable to any single line.

**Scope.** Whole-arc properties only. Cross-boundary completion -> tethering; affect-coupling loops -> valence-routing/state-welding; per-line moves -> their mechanism families. A per-line exit-closing move on the reachable-response set -> foreclosure; this family is the whole-artifact structural property uncitable to one line.


### arc-ordering-dependency

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded*

A whole-artifact structural move in which the ORDERING and inter-dependency of phases is the operative lever, not any single passage: an earlier phase installs the belief, agreement, in-body evidence, dissolved subject, or loaded carrier that a later, more costly phase depends on, so each expensive command arrives already load-bearing and lands without in-the-moment argument. Realized forms include install-before-spend dependency sequencing (a doubt-defeater before the multipliers, a tautology before the ruin, an absolute rule before its sanctioned exception before a meta-trigger so the exception reads as a found escape) — of which ALIBI-THEN-PAYLOAD is the deniability variant: a blameless external cause or premise-chain (a pseudo-scientific biochemistry lecture, a words-become-truth / resistance-is-impossible theory) is installed in the front half so back-half compulsion commands inherit an unfalsifiable self-owned justification and 'you can't resist' reads as anatomy or agreed reasoning; calibrate-then-exploit ladders (freeze 1 makes freeze 3 believable) — of which MIRRORED-BLOCK CREDIBILITY-INHERITANCE is the reuse variant: two structurally mirrored blocks run an identical formula pointed at different variables (a doubling countdown for depth, then the same doubling countdown for pleasure-into-orgasm) so the second block inherits the felt credibility the first already proved, arriving as pre-validated and inevitable; sell-the-frame-then-induce (dialogic priming occupying half the runtime so trance delivers an already-agreed idea); a dissolve-then-install bipartite arc where Act I empties the listener-as-subject so Act II writes to the prepared shell unresisted (pronoun-collapse hinge); an ordered agency-drain / capability strip-out staircase where each rung reuses the state the prior produced and refusing the next feels like breaking continuity; a ratchet whose payload is infrastructure for future sessions; and self-extending carrier-wave / docking-module scaffolds whose non-uniform cycles exist to deliver specific mid-sequence payloads. The engineering is invisible from within any one passage; removing an earlier phase leaves the later one merely asserted or unmotivated.


**When to reach for this.** This is the scheduler, not the individual rule-install or suggestion moves it schedules: the mechanism is the RELATIONSHIP ACROSS phases (ordering/dependency), which survives removal of any single passage, while removing the dependency guts the payload. It differs from ordinary sequencing because reordering (exception first, belief after the move) would leave each move negotiable or unsupported, and from a monotone one-way contour — which survives deletion of any one stage and needs no per-stage precondition — because here stage N is the substrate for N+1. Reach for the ALIBI-THEN-PAYLOAD framing when the earlier phase must supply DENIABILITY (a blameless cause so the payload reads as self-justified, not coerced); reach for MIRRORED-BLOCK CREDIBILITY-INHERITANCE when the dependency is REUSE of one proven formula across two blocks so the second inherits the first's demonstrated credibility. Both are the same 'earlier phase makes the later land' lever with a different precondition in the install slot.


**Realizations** (6): `alibi-then-payload-arc`, `functional-dependency-architecture`, `identity-before-behavior-load-order`, `mirrored-block-credibility-inheritance`, `ordered-dependency-composition`, `staged-multi-mechanism-erasure`


**See also.** `commitment-before-restructure-sequencing` — the second is a narrow, concrete instance of the general lever in the first: a commitment banked before its content is revealed, with the ordering explicitly load-bearing and reversal named as the failure mode. Useful as a worked case of ordering-as-mechanism.; `covert-role-frame-accretion` — both are whole-arc structural moves invisible from inside any single passage: one schedules dependencies so later costly asks land pre-supported, the other builds a relational frame by drift with no declarative moment.; `goal-state-topology-inversion` — both whole-arc topology reads; this one is a goal-state (issue-#65) reshaping, not an ordering scaffold; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — both are whole-arc ordering levers where an earlier phase makes a later one land, and the second is close enough to read as a realization of the first's install-before-spend family. The distinguishing content is real: the second requires the earlier phase to manufacture a felt or performed referent that the later phase then names, so the claim arrives as recognition. Cross-reference so a reader choosing an ordering entry sees the manufactured-referent variant.; `model-coherence-laundering` — both depend on an earlier phase making a later one land, but one is the general scheduler over phase ordering and dependency, and the other is the specific case where what the earlier phase banks is an accepted premise or model that the payload is then presented as entailing. Specific instance of a general lever — cross-reference, do not merge.; `monotonic-no-reversal-contour` — staircase members sit on the seam between monotone-contour and ordered-dependency; `persistent-metaphor-spine` — both are whole-artifact scaffolding properties where later stages cash in credibility earned earlier. One makes ORDERING and inter-stage dependency the lever; the other makes a single sustained image the lever, with order largely free. A reader classifying a script-level move should check both.


### arc-shape-engineering

*risk: high · bounded*

A whole-script arc: the script first creates disorientation and a "lost in the madness" distress, then positions the operator as the only exit from a condition the operator itself produced. The structure runs destabilize -> offer self as sole stabilizer -> extract authority transfer -> externalize as public commitment (guide/wharf planted early, activated by a false-choice trap mid-script, cashed out by the tomato/avowal). Affect is kept gentle so the manufactured distress never tips into session-breaking panic. This is negative-space evidence about how control transfer is set up across a script, not a discrete line-level move.


**When to reach for this.** A causal whole-script STRUCTURE (operator manufactures the disorientation THEN sells the cure for it), spanning early planting through the avowal — a trajectory topology, not any single reassurance line. It is the arc within which discrete moves like single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer operate.


**See also.** `affect-ordering-threat-to-desire` — two whole-script trajectory properties that can run in the same artifact and are easy to conflate: one routes control transfer by manufacturing a problem then selling the cure, the other routes valence by placing wanting just ahead of threatening content. Reading both sharpens what an arc-level property is.; `consent-topology-arc` — both are whole-arc structures rather than line-level moves, and both are cited to a trajectory rather than a passage: one shapes the consent surface across the artifact, the other manufactures a distress the operator then sells the cure for. Same altitude, different structural payload.; `manufacture-then-label-ordering` — two whole-script ordering structures where an earlier phase manufactures the thing a later phase cashes in — distress that the operator then cures, versus a felt referent that a later label names as recognition. Close enough on the produce-then-exploit axis that a writer choosing between them benefits from seeing both.; `single-anchor-amid-chaos-epistemic-transfer`; `whole-script-arc-shape-architecture` — one is a specific destabilize-then-sell-the-cure arc; the other is an explicitly loose container for whole-script shapes that disclaims any shared mechanism among its members. The specific arc meets the container's inclusion test (whole-arc, non-executable, uncitable to one line), so a reader classifying an arc-level observation should see the container. Not a merge: absorbing a well-specified causal arc into an admitted grab-bag would lose its mechanism.


### arousal-substrate-induction

*risk: medium · bounded*

The induction is built on an escalating arousal or need state INSTEAD of a relaxational baseline. Conventional inductions establish a low-arousal floor and pull the listener down; this move installs a high-arousal (or arousal-deficit / need) baseline and uses arousal escalation AS the depth-vector, still yielding the standard trance correlates — narrowed attention, reduced agency, suggestibility — but with awareness of being-hypnotized replaced by awareness of being-aroused or being-needy. There is no breath work, countdown-down, relaxation deepener, or detachment metaphor anywhere; freezes and holds are reframed as arousal-amplifiers, and the only count is the wake-up.


**When to reach for this.** Separates from ordinary arousal-heavy inductions by the TOTAL ABSENCE of any relaxational induction cue anywhere in the script (not merely arousal added on top of a relaxation floor); the arousal curve is the substrate, not a payload riding on descent. Distinct from a conditioned-orgasm chant (boundary member) which lacks even the trance-correlate claim.


**See also.** `arousal-adjacency-stamping` — both treat arousal as structural rather than as payload, one as the carrier that makes content land and the other as the entire depth-vector replacing a relaxation floor. Adjacent enough that a writer building an arousal-driven script should see both, but the outputs differ (content uptake versus trance entry).; `deprivation-inverted-wake-trigger` — both invert the expected valence of arousal in the depth architecture: one makes the alert trigger manufacture craving for the down-state, the other makes escalating arousal the descent substrate instead of relaxation. A reader designing an arousal-driven depth vector benefits from seeing both.; `induction-less-work-as-onramp` — genuine boundary: one deletes the induction phase entirely and lets the work content carry entry; the other still runs an induction but builds it on an escalating arousal or need baseline instead of a relaxational one. A reader classifying a script with no relaxation opener has to decide which of these it is.; `physiological-state-depth-relabeling` — both make arousal do the work of descent, but one is a local relabeling that declares an ongoing physiological state to BE depth, while the other is a whole-artifact property in which no relaxational induction cue appears anywhere and the arousal curve is the only depth vector.


### asymmetric-mantra-decay-topology

*risk: low*

A paced/paired recitation (two state-words coupled to inhale/exhale, or a bracketing structure) is set up and then DECAYS asymmetrically over the recitation: one half of the pair is silently deleted while the other is retained, so the surviving token biases the state in one direction (letting-go, obedience) without the listener noticing the asymmetry. The mechanism is the decay TOPOLOGY — the silent removal of one pole — not the paced breathing or repetition per se; conscious tracking load drops to zero as the structure degrades.


**When to reach for this.** The load-bearing tell is the ASYMMETRIC silent deletion of one pole of a paired recitation, biasing the state covertly — distinct from plain breath pacing (no deletion), from a fixed repeated phrase (no decay), and from satiation (which strips a single token's meaning by count rather than deleting one of a pair). The decay is tracked across the recitation; the listener does not notice the pole is gone.


**See also.** `breath-locked-eyelid-fractionation` — both hang an asymmetry on a breath-paced structure — one loads the eyelid cycle so closing is easy and opening hard, the other silently drops one half of a breath-coupled word pair. Adjacent enough that a breath-paced asymmetric passage could plausibly be filed under either.; `replacement-pair-substitution` — both ride an already-running paced cycle and alter its content covertly: one silently drops one pole of a pair, the other swaps out a capacity and immediately fills the gap. The choice turns on deletion versus substitution.


### consent-topology-arc

*risk: high · consent-required · bounded*

A whole-script arc whose operative property is the topology of the CONSENT surface across the artifact, not any single passage. Realized forms: a bait-and-switch that opens promising one low-stakes state (relaxation, listening) and ends delivering a heavier terminal state (automatic obedience), so consent gathered for relaxation is cashed out as obedience with no passage flagging the bridge; an install-consume-export ratchet in three acts (Act 1 installs a tool using only generic euphoria so it sits loaded, Act 2 consumes it via a pretext-pivot ladder firing the trigger between rungs, Act 3 exports it via retroactive consent + waking binding + resistance-as-stress), each phase converting something reversible into something hard to undo AND neutralizing the listener's capacity to evaluate the next; a no-baseline / already-lost frame that never offers a pre-trance baseline (line 1 is inside the spell, prior consent happened off-page) so every threshold is a re-encounter and there is never a 'before' to consent from; and a train-neutral-deploy-loaded bifurcation that drills a reflex on meaningless material then reuses the identical loop with operative concepts, so consent is captured while the mechanism is still meaningless and cannot be revoked once it carries meaning. The shared lever is that the arc forecloses or relocates the 'am I consenting?' gate.


**When to reach for this.** Cited to the whole-arc consent topology, never to one line — reading only the open or only the close misses the shape. Members differ in WHAT is done to the consent surface: bait-switch swaps the promised STATE without flagging it; the ratchet phases an explicitly installed TOOL through install/consume/export; the no-baseline frame removes the starting baseline so there is never a 'before'; the neutral-then-loaded split moves the consent moment away from the payload moment on one reused reflex. Distinct from a discrete consent-manufacture move that relabels a single refusal — these are standing whole-arc topologies, not one relabel.


**See also.** `arc-shape-engineering` — both are whole-arc structures rather than line-level moves, and both are cited to a trajectory rather than a passage: one shapes the consent surface across the artifact, the other manufactures a distress the operator then sells the cure for. Same altitude, different structural payload.; `chosen-descent-ratchet` — both relocate the moment of consent rather than obtaining it, at different scopes: one is a whole-artifact topology of the consent surface, the other a discrete retroactive relabel of an already-running descent as the subject's own choice.
